overview: The Medford Sustainability & MEP Systems Advisory Team met to review mechanical system options, lifecycle costs, and solar PV strategies for the Medford High School Project, tentatively endorsing an all-electric air-to-water heat pump system.

items.title: Meeting Introduction and Team Role
items.summary: Matt Rice introduced the team's advisory role in generating mechanical and sustainability recommendations for the upcoming October school building committee meeting.

items.title: Sustainability Goals and Requirements Refresher
items.summary: Martine Dion reviewed the project's baseline sustainability goals, including LEED Silver targets, specialized stretch energy code compliance, and city net-zero goals.

items.title: HVAC Lifecycle Cost Analysis (LCCA)
items.summary: The team analyzed a preliminary 50-year lifecycle cost study comparing 100% ground-source heat pumps, a hybrid geothermal/air-source system, and 100% air-to-water heat pumps against a fossil fuel baseline.

items.title: Mechanical System Technical and Phasing Assessment
items.summary: Emily Ehlers explained the physical layouts, maintenance lifespans, roof footprints, and multi-phase construction challenges of each mechanical system option.

items.title: HVAC System Advisory Selection
items.summary: The advisory team reached a unanimous tentative recommendation to support Option 3, the 100% air-to-water heat pump system, due to lower upfront costs, simpler maintenance, and less disruptive phasing.

items.title: Preliminary Photovoltaic (PV) System Assessment
items.summary: Martine Dion presented preliminary solar PV output assessments for roof and parking canopy locations, contrasting the economics of third-party power purchase agreements with city ownership.
